items.title: Tony Marino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 25, 2025
items.q: Hal Galper, when I play with him about the big beat.

ctx.x: Do you have a spot on stage that you usually like to stand? I know some – I’ve heard bass players saying, “Well I want to be on your hi-hat side” or something like that.

Yeah a lot of guys are that way. I like to be in the middle for sure, between whatever the chordal instrument is and the drums, and I don’t have to be on the hi-hat side. When I’m locking in my time, I’m listening to what the right hand or – not everybody is a right handed drummer – but the time. Where the quarter note is coming from if we’re playing swing and jazz. You know? I want to know – that’s where I get the time from, his hands, © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

more than that hi-hat two and four. You know. So I’m listening for that. And that lets me know if I’m in sync with his quarter note, if I’m a little behind I’m a little bit – and every drummer’s different. You know I play with guys that really are on top of the beat and you’ve really gotta push. And then you get used to playing with a guy like that, then you’re playing with someone that plays a little behind the beat and you’re pushing him and you don’t want to push him. You know? You want to relax and breathe.…
